note: Absolute radial check against the lunar laser ranging (LLR) retroreflectors, independent of LOLA. Written and committed BEFORE any DEM value at a reflector was looked at; not to be edited afterwards. The commit time is the authoritative time of writing.

DE421.citation: J. G. Williams, D. H. Boggs, W. M. Folkner, DE421 Lunar Orbit, Physical Librations, and Surface Coordinates, JPL IOM 335-JW,DB,WF-20080314-001, 14 March 2008, Table 4 (mean Earth/mean rotation axis frame) and eq. (3)

DE430.citation: J. G. Williams, D. H. Boggs, W. M. Folkner, DE430 Lunar Orbit, Physical Librations, and Surface Coordinates, JPL IOM 335-JW,DB,WF-20130722-016, 22 July 2013, Table 7 (mean Earth/mean rotation axis frame), Tables 6 and 8, eqs. (4)-(5)

frame.our_products: LOLA labels: COORDINATE_SYSTEM_NAME = 'MEAN EARTH/POLAR AXIS OF DE421', planetocentric, sphere 1737.4 km
frame.choice: DE421 Table 4 is in exactly that frame and is used for Apollo 11, 14, 15 and Lunokhod 2. Lunokhod 1 was not in DE421 (recovered in 2010); its coordinates are taken from DE430 Table 7. DE430's MER frame was aligned to the DE421 one (memo section 6.1); for the four common arrays DE430 - DE421 differ by about 1.5 m horizontally and 0.4 m in radius, far below the DEM's resolution. No conversion is applied to DE421 Table 4; the PA coordinates (DE421 Table 3) are evaluated as well, only to show the size of a PA/ME mix-up (about 830 m horizontally).
frame.tide: the tabulated positions exclude the constant tidal displacement (DE421 Table 5: +0.19 to +0.42 m radial); not added, it is below the DEM's precision

expected_agreement.difference: d = r_DEM(lon, lat) - r_reflector, bilinear DEM radius at the reflector's latitude and longitude
expected_agreement.what_the_DEM_allows: a reflector stands on the surface: Apollo arrays about 0.3-0.5 m above the ground, the Lunokhod reflectors on the rover body, about 1-2 m (not measured here), so d should be slightly negative. The DEM value is an average over a pixel (118 m for SLDEM2015_256, 237 m for LDEM_128, 1.9 km for LDEM_16) and its absolute radius is good to the LOLA radial accuracy (published: ~10 m in 2010, orbits <10 m in total after GRAIL). The pixel-scale relief is measured from the DEM itself, without the reflector: sigma_local = RMS deviation of the 3 x 3 pixels around the reflector from their mean.
expected_agreement.pass_if: |d| <= tolerance for all five reflectors on SLDEM2015_256 and on LDEM_128 (LDEM_16 reported only)
frame_or_radius_problem_if: all five d of the same sign with |mean d| > 10 m: a radius or datum problem (for example a 1737.151 km instead of 1737.4 km reference would give about -250 m; a km/m slip thousands of metres)
|d| much larger than the tolerance at one or two reflectors while d at the PA positions is small there: a PA/ME or longitude-convention problem
expected_agreement.not_testable: horizontal position: at these sites a 100 m horizontal error changes the DEM height by about slope * 100 m, i.e. a few metres on the mare, inside the tolerance; this check constrains the radius and the reference sphere, not the horizontal frame
